claim: Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null) encodes a false invariant and fires on legitimate, already-tested no-rowid paths (composite PK, WITHOUT ROWID, views, expression columns) in Debug builds
raw: `Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null)` now encodes a false invariant and fires on legitimate, already-tested code paths. The old assert was trivially true (`_rowidOrdinal` was pre-seeded to `-1` before the scan); the new variable starts `null` and is only assigned when a rowid **is** found.

claim: Negative-result caching was dropped: RowIds.Add only runs on success, so fallback-path tables re-run the full column scan plus a pragma_table_info SQL round trip on every GetStream call (per chunk in chunked GetBytes)
raw: Negative-result caching was silently dropped: `RowIds.Add` is only called in the two success branches (lines 355, 387), so when no rowid/single-PK column is found, nothing is cached and every subsequent `GetStream` call re-runs the full `FieldCount` scan

claim: Fix is incomplete for self-joins: sqlite3_column_table_name returns the origin table not the alias, so both aliases share one cache key and the second alias silently gets the wrong row's blob
raw: `sqlite3_column_table_name` returns the *origin* table, not the FROM-clause alias, so in `SELECT a1.VALUE, a2.VALUE FROM A a1 JOIN A a2 ON ...` both blob columns share one cache key (`main_A`). The first alias's rowid ordinal is cached and silently reused for the second alias

claim: Cache key $"{db}_{table}" is collision-prone since '_' is legal in SQLite database and table names; on collision the wrong table's rowid ordinal is reused, silently returning another row's BLOB
raw: Cache key `$"{blobDatabaseName}_{blobTableName}"` is a delimiter-joined composite with collision potential: `_` is legal in SQLite database (ATTACH alias) and table names, so `(main, A_B)` and `(main_A, B)` both produce `main_A_B`.

claim: RowIdInfo is an overbuilt mutable cache-entry type: TableName is write-only dead state, public setters on write-once data, reduces to an int, and cannot represent 'scanned, not found'
raw: `RowIdInfo` is an overbuilt, mutable cache-entry type: `TableName` is write-only dead state (assigned at lines 354/386, never read anywhere — grep-verified; the `SqliteBlob` construction uses the `blobTableName` local instead), both properties have public setters despite write-once usage

claim: New test covers only the reported repro and has hygiene defects: no Assert.IsType<SqliteBlob>, Console.WriteLine debris, unasserted ID values, missing self-join/ATTACH/reverse-order/multi-row/fallback-join scenarios
raw: it never pins the streaming path with `Assert.IsType<SqliteBlob>` (neighboring tests do), so a silent regression to the whole-blob `MemoryStream` fallback still passes; (b) `Console.WriteLine` at line 171 is the only one in the file — debug debris

claim: RowIds field violates file conventions: PascalCase without access modifier vs private _camelCase siblings, and eagerly allocated per record instead of lazily like every sibling cache
raw: every sibling field is `private` + `_camelCase` (`_blobCache`, `_columnNameOrdinalCache`, …) and every sibling *cache* is a nullable field lazily allocated on first use, while `RowIds` is PascalCase, omits the access modifier, and is eagerly allocated per `SqliteDataRecord`

claim: New comments narrate change history or misdescribe the code ('this was failing. now should be fixed', 'get len of abuff') while the non-obvious production decisions carry no comments at all
raw: `//this was failing. now should be fixed` (test:179) states no invariant and rots immediately; `//get len of abuff` (test:173) sits above a fixed-size buffer allocation, not a length computation

claim: Style nits: stray whitespace-only line after namespace brace (17), missing spaces around != (393), rowidkey breaks camelCase (328)
raw: a stray whitespace-only line right after the `namespace` opening brace (line 17); `rowIdForOrdinal!=null` lacks spaces around `!=` (line 393), unlike surrounding code; local `rowidkey` breaks camelCase (`rowIdKey`) at line 328.

claim: Re-added Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal != null) fires on legitimate fallback paths; existing tests GetStream_works and GetStream_works_when_composite_pk drive this path, crashing Debug-configuration test runs
raw: The old assert (`Debug.Assert(_rowidOrdinal.HasValue)`) was trivially true because `_rowidOrdinal` was set to `-1` before the scan. The commit message says "assert readded," but the re-added form asserts a condition that is genuinely false whenever no rowid is resolvable

claim: Negative caching removed: fallback-path reads re-run the full scan plus a fresh pragma_table_info SQL command on every GetStream call — per chunk per row in the standard chunked GetBytes pattern
raw: The old code cached `_rowidOrdinal = -1` before scanning, so the scan (per-column `sqlite3_table_column_metadata` calls plus the `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_table_info($table)` command at lines 375–381) ran at most once per result set. The new code only inserts into `RowIds` on success

claim: Fix incomplete for self-joins: all aliases of the same table share one cache key, so the first alias's rowid ordinal is silently reused for the second alias — SqliteBlob returns the wrong row's blob
raw: The cache is keyed by origin database + table name. `sqlite3_column_table_name` returns the *origin* table, not the FROM-clause alias, so in `SELECT a1.ID, a1.VALUE, a2.ID, a2.VALUE FROM A a1 JOIN A a2 ON ...` all four columns report table `A` and share one cache key.

claim: Brittle string cache key $"{db}_{table}" — '_' is a legal identifier character so distinct (database, table) pairs collide, silently returning wrong blob data
raw: `_` is a legal identifier character in both database aliases (`ATTACH ... AS main_a`) and table names, so (`main`, `A_B`) and (`main_A`, `B`) produce the identical key `main_A_B`. Null database/table (expression columns) both collapse to `"_"`.

claim: New test does not pin the streaming path with Assert.IsType<SqliteBlob>, contains Console.WriteLine debris with no assertion, and misses reverse-order, mixed one-table-fallback, multi-row, and self-join scenarios
raw: The test is named `GetBytes_works_streaming_join` but never asserts the stream type. Every neighboring test pins the path with `Assert.IsType<SqliteBlob>` / `Assert.IsType<MemoryStream>` (e.g., lines 478, 533); this one only checks byte values

claim: RowIds/RowIdInfo break every established pattern in the file: dead write-only TableName, PascalCase field without private modifier, eager allocation, stray blank line 17, unspaced != at 393
raw: `RowIdInfo.TableName` is stored and never read anywhere (grep-verified) — dead weight with public mutable setters. The field `RowIds` lacks `private`, is PascalCase where every sibling is `_camelCase` (`_blobCache`, `_typeCache`), and is eagerly allocated per `SqliteDataRecord`

claim: Debug.Assert now encodes a false invariant and fires on an existing, correctly-handled code path (composite PK / WITHOUT ROWID), exercised by pre-existing test GetStream_works_when_composite_pk
raw: In the old code, `_rowidOrdinal` was pre-seeded to `-1` before the scan loop, so `Debug.Assert(_rowidOrdinal.HasValue)` was trivially always true regardless of whether a rowid was actually found — it asserted nothing meaningful. In the new code `rowIdForOrdinal` starts as `null`

claim: Negative lookup result is never cached, causing repeated full table scans plus extra pragma_table_info SQL round-trips on every GetStream call for tables with no usable rowid
raw: `RowIds.Add(rowidkey, rowIdForOrdinal)` is only called inside the two `break` branches. When no rowid/single-PK column is found (composite PK, view, `WITHOUT ROWID` table), nothing is stored under `rowidkey`. Every subsequent `GetStream` call therefore re-runs the full scan

claim: Dictionary key built by naive string concatenation risks collisions between distinct tables, silently reusing a RowIdInfo computed for the wrong table — a data-correctness bug
raw: Because `_` is both the separator and a legal character in SQLite identifiers, two different `(database, table)` pairs can produce the same key — e.g. database `main`, table `foo_bar` vs. database `main_foo`, table `bar` both yield `"main_foo_bar"`.

claim: New RowIds field doesn't follow the file's private-field naming convention (private _camelCase); it uses PascalCase with no explicit access modifier
raw: Every other field in this class is declared `private` and `_camelCase` (`_connection`, `_addChanges`, `_blobCache`, `_typeCache`, `_columnNameOrdinalCache`, `_columnNameCache`, `_stepped`, `_alreadyThrown`, `_alreadyAddedChanges`). `RowIds` uses PascalCase with no explicit access modifier

claim: Local variable rowidkey breaks camelCase, inconsistent with sibling locals in the same method; should be rowIdKey
raw: `rowidkey` breaks camelCase, unlike sibling locals in the same method (`blobDatabaseName`, `blobTableName`, `blobColumnName`, `pkColumns`). Should be `rowIdKey`.

claim: RowIdInfo.TableName is set but never read anywhere — dead data that adds confusion about what distinguishes cache entries
raw: Verified via grep — `TableName` is assigned in the constructor and at both call sites but never consumed anywhere else in the codebase. It's dead data that adds confusion about what actually distinguishes cache entries

claim: Leftover Console.WriteLine debug output and a history-narrating comment ('this was failing. now should be fixed') in the new test
raw: This is the only `Console.WriteLine` in the entire test file — looks like a leftover debugging artifact rather than an intentional assertion, and the comment narrates the bug-fix history rather than describing current behavior

claim: Self-join reintroduces the exact bug class this PR fixes and is completely untested: both aliases compute the same RowIds key so the second blob column reuses the wrong cached ordinal
raw: `sqlite3_column_table_name` returns the *un-aliased* origin table name, not the query alias. In a self-join (`SELECT a.blob, b.blob FROM T a JOIN T b ON ...`), both blob columns resolve to the same `blobTableName` ("T") and, typically, the same `blobDatabaseName` ("main")

claim: Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null) now fires on a legitimate not-found path, and the pre-existing GetStream_works_when_composite_pk test already exercises it — Debug builds can FailFast the test process
raw: The OLD code set `_rowidOrdinal = -1` as a sentinel before scanning, so `Debug.Assert(_rowidOrdinal.HasValue)` always passed even when no rowid/PK-alias column was found (composite PK case). The NEW code leaves `rowIdForOrdinal` as `null` in that same case

claim: Dictionary key collision from naive string concatenation (db + '_' + table): distinct pairs can collide; a tuple key would eliminate the bug class
raw: Because both segments are freeform SQLite identifiers that can themselves contain underscores, two different `(database, table)` pairs can collide: e.g. database `"a_b"` + table `"c"` produces the same key as database `"a"` + table `"b_c"`.

claim: ATTACH'ed database with a same-named table — the database half of the fix's own db_table key design — is completely unexercised by tests
raw: The new key format is `database_table` specifically to disambiguate by database as well as table — but the new test only varies the table half (`A` vs `B` in the default `main` database); it never proves the database half works.

claim: No test proves the fix works in reverse — re-reading table A's blob after B's entry has been cached (the most literal regression check for the reported symptom)
raw: The new test reads table A's blob once, then table B's blob once — each hitting a cache-miss populate exactly once. It never re-reads table A's blob *after* B's entry has been cached

claim: No multi-row loop through the joined/cached path — nothing proves cached entries stay valid across multiple rows of a joined query
raw: Every `GetStream`/blob test in the file (new and pre-existing) reads a single row. The dictionary is populated once and then presumably reused across `reader.Read()` iterations in real usage, but nothing in the suite proves the cached entries stay valid/correct across multiple rows

claim: A single-column INTEGER PK on a WITHOUT ROWID table satisfies the pkColumns==1 branch and is treated as a rowid alias, but sqlite3_blob_open would fail at runtime — pre-existing, untested
raw: A single-column PK on a `WITHOUT ROWID` table can satisfy `dataType=="INTEGER" && primaryKey!=0 && pkColumns==1`, causing the code to treat it as a rowid-alias and construct a `SqliteBlob` using that value as a rowid — but `WITHOUT ROWID` tables have no rowid, so `sqlite3_blob_open` would fail

claim: Expression/computed blob column (empty db/table name, key '_') alongside a join is unexercised; two expression-derived blob columns would share key '_'
raw: An expression column has empty `blobDatabaseName`/`blobTableName`, producing key `"_"`. Not-found is the correct outcome (fall back to `GetCachedBlob`), but this exercises the same `Debug.Assert` problem as gap #2

claim: Debug output left in test code: Console.WriteLine at line 171 is the only one in the file, inconsistent with repo conventions and adds no verification value
raw: **Debug output left in production test code** — `Console.WriteLine($"A.ID={reader.GetInt32(0)} B.ID={reader.GetInt32(2)}");` at line 171. This is the only `Console.WriteLine` in the entire `SqliteDataReaderTest.cs` file (confirmed via grep across the file)

claim: GetInt32 values are never checked with Assert.Equal despite the comment's claim — the test only proves the calls don't throw and silently accepts wrong values
raw: the comment above the `Console.WriteLine` claims "reading fields that does not involve blobs should be ok," but the returned `GetInt32` values are never checked with `Assert.Equal`. As written, the test only proves those calls don't throw

claim: Stale/misleading comment '//get len of abuff' sits above a fixed-size buffer allocation, not a length computation
raw: `//get len of abuff` above `var abuff = new byte[2];` doesn't describe what the code does (it allocates a fixed 2-byte buffer, not "get a length")

claim: Vague regression-test annotation '//this was failing. now should be fixed' narrates change history without pointing at the issue or describing the regression
raw: `//this was failing. now should be fixed` narrates change history without pointing at the issue (repo convention elsewhere favors linking a specific bug, or at minimum the comment should say what the regression *is* rather than "now should be fixed")

claim: Self-joins collide on the same RowIds cache key because sqlite3_column_table_name reports the underlying table, not the alias — the second blob column silently returns blob data from the wrong row
raw: Self-joins (same table referenced twice via aliases) collide on the same RowIds cache key ($"{blobDatabaseName}_{blobTableName}"), because sqlite3_column_table_name reports the underlying table name, not the query alias. The second blob column's GetStream call reuses the first alias's cached ordinal

claim: The 'no derivable rowid' result is no longer cached, causing repeated full rescans with a nested SQL query, and Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null) can now genuinely fire for common, already-tested query shapes
raw: The 'no derivable rowid' outcome is no longer cached (unlike the old sentinel-based code), so every GetStream/GetBytes/GetChars call on such a column re-runs the full scan plus a nested SQL round trip, and Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null) now evaluates a genuinely false condition

claim: rowidkey uses a plain underscore delimiter with no escaping, so distinct (database, table) pairs can collide — retained as a low-confidence observation (~50, below JSON threshold)
raw: `rowidkey = $"{blobDatabaseName}_{blobTableName}"` uses a plain underscore delimiter with no escaping, so distinct `(database, table)` pairs can collide, e.g. database `"a"` + table `"b_c"` and database `"a_b"` + table `"c"` both produce `"a_b_c"`

claim: Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null) is no longer tautological and now genuinely fires for any table without a discoverable rowid — a scenario the very next line handles as a legitimate outcome
raw: In the old code, `_rowidOrdinal = -1;` was set as a sentinel *before* the discovery loop ran, so `Debug.Assert(_rowidOrdinal.HasValue)` afterward was always true regardless of whether a rowid was actually found — it was a no-op assertion by construction.

claim: The 'no rowid found' result is no longer cached, causing the full discovery loop and a live pragma_table_info SQL query to re-run on every GetStream call
raw: `RowIds.Add(rowidkey, rowIdForOrdinal)` (lines 355, 387) is only invoked inside the two success branches. When no rowid/single-column PK is found, nothing is added to `RowIds`, so on the *next* call to `GetStream` for that same table/column the `RowIds.TryGetValue` check misses again

claim: Cache key built by naive string concatenation can collide between distinct database/table pairs, causing lookup of the wrong RowIdInfo and a silently incorrect SqliteBlob handle
raw: `string rowidkey = $"{blobDatabaseName}_{blobTableName}";` has no unambiguous delimiter. A table named `"A_B"` in a database named `"main"` produces the same key (`"main_A_B"`) as a table `"B"` in a database named `"main_A"`

claim: New field RowIds breaks the private-field naming convention (_camelCase) used everywhere else in the class; PascalCase with no explicit access modifier
raw: The new field is declared as `readonly Dictionary<string, RowIdInfo> RowIds = new Dictionary<string, RowIdInfo>();` — PascalCase, with no explicit access modifier — which reads like a public property/field at a glance and is inconsistent with the rest of the same file.

claim: The refactor lost negative-result caching and the null sentinel conflates 'not yet scanned' with 'scanned, no rowid found'; the Debug.Assert now documents an invariant that is false by design
raw: The old code set `_rowidOrdinal = -1` before scanning, so "no usable rowid exists" (WITHOUT ROWID tables, views, expression columns, composite PKs) was cached once. The new code only calls `RowIds.Add(...)` on success, so for tables with no rowid, `TryGetValue` misses on **every** call.

claim: Cache key $"{db}_{table}" is a delimiter-joined composite with collision potential — on collision SqliteBlob is fed the wrong rowid, silently returning blob data from the wrong row/table
raw: `_` is legal in both SQLite schema (attached database) names and table names, so (`a_b`, `c`) and (`a`, `b_c`) map to the same key `a_b_c`. On collision the cached ordinal of one table's rowid is reused for a different table

claim: RowIdInfo is a single-use mutable class whose TableName property is never read — dead state duplicating the dictionary key; the whole type reduces to an int
raw: The only member consumed anywhere is `Ordinal` (line 402); `TableName` is assigned (lines 354, 386) and never read — dead state that a maintainer must reason about (is it load-bearing? does it need to match the key?). The table identity already lives in the dictionary key

claim: RowIds field breaks the file's lazy-allocation cache pattern (eagerly allocated per query execution even when GetStream is never called) and its private-field naming conventions
raw: Every other cache in this class (`_blobCache`, `_typeCache`, `_columnNameOrdinalCache`, `_columnNameCache`) is a nullable `_camelCase` private field allocated on first use (`_blobCache ??= ...` at line ~490). `RowIds` is eagerly allocated in the initializer for every `SqliteDataRecord`

claim: Rowid cache key with ambiguous '_' delimiter lets distinct (database, table) pairs collide; on collision SqliteBlob opens the correct table at the wrong row — wrong-row BLOB data disclosure within the connection's own database
raw: The scan loop itself compares `databaseName`/`tableName` individually and correctly (lines 340, 346), but on a key collision `RowIds.TryGetValue` (line 329) short-circuits that scan and returns the *other* table's `RowIdInfo`.

claim: Debug-build assertion regression: the rewritten Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal != null) now actually fires for legitimate cases the MemoryStream fallback is designed to handle; Debug/source builds and test runs can fail-fast on valid usage
raw: The old `Debug.Assert(_rowidOrdinal.HasValue)` was vacuous (the field was pre-set to `-1`). The rewritten `Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal != null)` now actually fires in Debug builds for legitimate cases the `MemoryStream` fallback (line 396–399) is designed to handle

claim: Negative-result caching removed (resource churn): a failed scan caches nothing, so every GetStream/GetBytes call re-runs the full column scan and re-executes the pragma_table_info COUNT query — a performance regression, not a vulnerability
raw: previously `_rowidOrdinal = -1` cached "no rowid found"; now a failed scan caches nothing, so every `GetStream`/`GetBytes` call on such a table's blob (per row, per column) re-runs the full column scan including `sqlite3_table_column_metadata` calls

claim: Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null) silently changed meaning and is undocumented — it now fires whenever no rowid is found, a path the pre-existing GetStream_works_when_composite_pk test exercises
raw: `Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null)` silently changed meaning and is undocumented. In the old code, `_rowidOrdinal` was unconditionally set to the sentinel `-1` *before* the search loop ran, so `Debug.Assert(_rowidOrdinal.HasValue)` was always true — it never actually verified anything.

claim: '//this was failing. now should be fixed' narrates change history with zero technical content — meaningless once merged and useless for diagnosing a future regression
raw: `//this was failing. now should be fixed` — narrates change history with zero technical content. It doesn't say *what* was failing, *why*, or what scenario the test is guarding against (a shared/incorrectly-cached rowid ordinal when two tables are joined).

claim: '//reading fields that does not involve blobs should be ok' has a grammar error and overstates what the test confirms — the claim is only checked implicitly, with no assertion
raw: `//reading fields that does not involve blobs should be ok` has a subject-verb agreement error ("fields... does" → "do"), and more importantly the code beneath it (`Console.WriteLine(...)`) has no assertion — the "should be ok" claim is only checked implicitly

claim: The new RowIds dictionary and its underscore-delimited key format are completely undocumented, including a real (if narrow) collision risk that no comment acknowledges and the code doesn't guard against
raw: The new `RowIds` dictionary and its key format (`$"{blobDatabaseName}_{blobTableName}"`) are completely undocumented. This is exactly the kind of non-obvious design decision that needs a comment

claim: RowIdInfo has no comment explaining its purpose, and TableName is set but never read — a future maintainer cannot tell whether it is vestigial or load-bearing
raw: New internal type with no comment explaining its purpose. Additionally, `TableName` is set in the constructor and stored, but grep confirms it is never read anywhere in the file — it's dead data carried on every cache entry.

claim: When no rowid ordinal is found the result is not added to RowIds — every subsequent GetStream/GetBytes call re-runs the full loop plus metadata calls and a pragma_table_info query; nothing documents this trade-off
raw: When no rowid/PK ordinal is found for a table (the composite-PK / WITHOUT ROWID case), the result is *not* added to `RowIds`. Previously `_rowidOrdinal = -1` permanently cached the negative result for the whole `SqliteDataRecord`.

claim: '//get len of abuff' actively misdescribes the code (fixed-size buffer declaration, not a length computation) and should be removed
raw: `//get len of abuff` sits directly above `var abuff = new byte[2];` — a fixed-size buffer declaration, not any "length" computation. The comment doesn't describe what the line does

claim: Negative-cache invariant is broken: 'no rowid' is representable only by absence from the dictionary, so nothing is ever cached for no-rowid tables and the full scan plus pragma_table_info query re-runs per row
raw: Only the two `break` paths (`rowid`-alias found, or single-column INTEGER PK found) call `RowIds.Add(...)`. If a blob column's table is `WITHOUT ROWID`, has a composite primary key, or is a view, the loop finishes with `rowIdForOrdinal == null` and **nothing is ever added to `RowIds` for that key**.

claim: RowIdInfo.TableName is write-only dead state — set in the constructor, never read; SqliteBlob construction uses the blobTableName local instead — a bug magnet and needless per-entry allocation
raw: Grep of the whole file (and `test/`) shows `TableName` is set in the constructor (line 28) and never read anywhere afterward. The `SqliteBlob` construction at line 404 uses the original `blobTableName` local, not `rowIdForOrdinal.TableName`.

claim: Dictionary key is a non-injective string concatenation — distinct (db, table) pairs collide, returning the wrong Ordinal/rowid pairing for a blob read (silent wrong-row/wrong-column risk); confidence 65
raw: `$"{blobDatabaseName}_{blobTableName}"` collapses two independent identifiers into one string with `_` as separator. SQLite table/database identifiers may legally contain `_` (quoted or not), so `(db="main_t", table="1")` and `(db="main", table="t_1")` both produce key `"main_t_1"`

claim: Unnecessary settable properties on a cache-entry type: Ordinal/TableName are { get; set; } though every site treats RowIdInfo as immutable — a future edit could mutate a shared entry and corrupt the cache with no signal
raw: `Ordinal`/`TableName` are `{ get; set; }` (lines 22-23) even though every construction site treats `RowIdInfo` as immutable — created once, inserted, read via `.Ordinal` only. Nothing in the type communicates "this is a fixed cache entry"

claim: Wrong tool for the job: a mutable reference-type class where a readonly record struct or tuple fits better — the class takes 12 lines to express what is effectively an int
raw: `RowIdInfo` has no behavior, two fields, and (once #2 is fixed) really only needs to carry one `int`. A `readonly record struct RowIdInfo(int Ordinal, string TableName)` (or, after dropping `TableName`, simply `Dictionary<string, int>`) would: express immutability at compile time

claim: RowIds breaks the file's (and sibling files') private _camelCase field convention — PascalCase with no explicit private modifier, conventionally signaling public API surface
raw: Every other instance field in this class (`_connection`, `_addChanges`, `_blobCache`, `_typeCache`, `_columnNameOrdinalCache`, `_columnNameCache`, `_stepped`, `_alreadyThrown`, `_alreadyAddedChanges`) is `private` + `_camelCase`. `RowIds` (line 39) has neither

claim: Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null) (no spaces, compiled out in Release) papers over the negative-cache gap: fires in Debug for legitimate no-rowid tables, silently masks the missed-cache case in Release
raw: In Debug builds it will now actually *fire* for legitimate no-rowid tables (regression vs. the old vacuous assert, which always held because of the `-1` sentinel); in Release it silently falls through to the `MemoryStream` fallback, masking the missed-cache case

claim: Stray blank line with trailing whitespace introduced right after the namespace opening brace — cosmetic only
raw: Stray blank line with trailing whitespace introduced right after the `namespace` opening brace. Cosmetic only.

claim: New RowIds field has no explicit access modifier and uses PascalCase naming, inconsistent with the surrounding _camelCase private-field convention
raw: the new `RowIds` field has no explicit access modifier (defaults to `private`, which is correct) but uses PascalCase naming, inconsistent with the surrounding `_camelCase` private-field convention in this file (e.g., `_blobCache`, `_columnNameCache`).

claim: Minor style nits: stray blank line after the namespace opening brace (17) and Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null) lacks spaces around != (396)
raw: a stray blank line added right after the `namespace` opening brace (`SqliteDataRecord.cs:17`), and `Debug.Assert(rowIdForOrdinal!=null)` (`SqliteDataRecord.cs:396`) lacks spaces around `!=`, unlike existing code style.

claim: RowIds.TryGetValue with a pre-declared out variable could use the out var idiom — a trivial simplification, not a correctness issue
raw: `RowIds.TryGetValue(rowidkey, out rowIdForOrdinal)` pattern (`SqliteDataRecord.cs:329`) reimplements what could be `RowIds.TryGetValue(rowidkey, out var rowIdForOrdinal)` — a trivial idiom simplification, not a correctness issue.
